# Hugging Face startup fix v1.9.1

## Root cause

The deployed `server.js` imported `./mediaJobRoutes`, but the file was not uploaded to the Hugging Face Space. The backend stopped before listening, so the Space reported `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

The deployment also needed the complete relative dependency chain, including the previously absent `azureClient.js` compatibility module.

## Upload all backend files together

Upload or replace these files in the same backend directory:

```text
server.js
azureClient.js
azureMediaProvider.js
azureMediaRoutes.js
mediaJobRoutes.js
mediaJobStore.js
privateMediaStorage.js
backgroundRemovalProvider.js
mediaWorker.js
creditLedger.js
orderLedger.js
workspaceStore.js
trialQuotaStore.js
projectStore.js
assetStore.js
marketplaceStore.js
licenseTemplateStore.js
sessionStore.js
marketplaceEntitlementStore.js
collaborationStore.js
projectRevisionStore.js
supabaseShadowRead.js
package.json
package-lock.json
.env.media-jobs.example
migrations/006_media_jobs_and_artifacts.sql
```

Keep existing data files, frontend assets, and all pre-existing backend modules in the Space. Do not upload `.env` files containing secrets.

## Required Hugging Face Secret names

```text
AZURE_API_KEY
AZURE_IMAGE_ENDPOINT=https://prakashsuvedi-7749-resource.services.ai.azure.com/openai/v1
AZURE_IMAGE_MODEL=gpt-image-1.5
AZURE_IMAGE_AUTH_MODE=api-key
AZURE_SORA_ENDPOINT=https://prakashsuvedi-7749-resource.services.ai.azure.com
AZURE_SORA_DEPLOYMENT_NAME=sora-2
AZURE_SORA_MODEL=sora-2
AZURE_SORA_API_VERSION=preview
AZURE_SORA_API_STYLE=foundry-v1
```

## Validation

The complete local CommonJS require chain now resolves under Node 18. `node --check` passed for `azureClient.js`, `azureMediaProvider.js`, `azureMediaRoutes.js`, `mediaJobRoutes.js`, `mediaJobStore.js`, `privateMediaStorage.js`, `mediaWorker.js`, and `server.js`.

Keep media jobs, private storage, and worker flags disabled until the full Space starts successfully and the admin provider tests pass.

content:
## Serious verification result

The live platform is **not running the backend package I prepared**. I verified the live Hugging Face health endpoint and it still reports:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "version": "1.7.0",
  "azureMaiImage": true,
  "azureSoraVideo": true
}
```

I also verified that the live server returns:

```text
Cannot GET /api/video/azure
```

That confirms the Sora route is absent from the running deployment. Therefore, the current failures are not caused by the Azure project ID or your Sora/gpt-image-1.5 resource URLs. The Space is serving the old backend.

### Why each action fails

| Action | Current result | Verified reason |
|---|---:|---|
| Sora generation | 404 | Live backend v1.7.0 has no `/api/video/azure` route |
| gpt-image premium | 402 | Existing old credit/entitlement gate rejects the request before the corrected adapter runs |
| gpt-image request | 400 | Old image route does not understand the corrected gpt-image-1.5 contract and payload |
| Admin testing | Controlled mode | The running frontend/backend combination is not using the new admin-aware provider flow, or the admin session headers are not reaching the new routes |

## What must happen before production testing

Deploy the complete backend package into the Hugging Face Space root—not only `server.js` and not inside a nested ZIP folder. The package must include:

```text
server.js
azureClient.js
azureMediaProvider.js
azureMediaRoutes.js
mediaJobRoutes.js
mediaJobStore.js
privateMediaStorage.js
backgroundRemovalProvider.js
mediaWorker.js
all existing store *.js files
package.json
package-lock.json
```

After the Space rebuilds, open:

```text
https://prakashsuvedi-nepalai-studio.hf.space/api/health
```

Do not test the generators until the response version changes from `1.7.0` to the new backend release. Then verify the route exists by testing from the application; a browser `GET` may still show `Cannot GET` because the route is intentionally `POST` only, but the application’s `POST` request must no longer return 404.

### Important correction to the earlier deployment guidance

The previous package delivery was not sufficient if only selected files were uploaded. The actual live health response proves the Space did not receive—or is not running—the corrected `server.js` and route modules. I cannot honestly claim that Azure image or Sora generation is production-ready until the live health version changes and one real Admin Workspace preview request succeeds.

Use the attached complete ZIP, extract its contents directly beside the existing `server.js`, commit all changed files, wait for the build and runtime restart, and then send me the new `/api/health` response. That response is the first objective production gate.
